problem: The factor is wrong. 1 cm²/s = 10⁻⁴ m²/s, and Ha takes the square root of D_A, so entering D_A in cm²/s instead of m²/s makes Ha 100 times too big (or 100 times too small if k_L is entered in cm/s), not 10 times.
fix: Mixing cm²/s with m/s shifts Ha by a factor of 100, because 1 cm²/s = 10⁻⁴ m²/s and the square root halves that power of ten. A factor of 100 can flip the regime.

problem: The tower height falls by the factor E only when the liquid film controls the overall rate. If the gas film carries most of the resistance, the same E in the liquid hardly changes the overall coefficient or the HTU, and a student will expect a ten-fold shorter tower in every case.
fix: The liquid-film resistance drops from 1/k_L to 1/(E·k_L), so the HTU falls by about E only when the liquid film controls; with strong gas-film resistance the height hardly changes.

problem: The 'slow reaction' curve 1 − 1.5x + 0.5x² has slope −1.5 at x = 0, so it draws an enhancement factor of 1.5. The table and caption call this case slow with E ≈ 1, so the picture contradicts the text.
fix: Use a nearly straight curve, for example 1 − 1.05x + 0.05x², whose interface slope is −1.05 and which matches the E ≈ 1 slow regime.

problem: The table jumps from fast pseudo-first-order to instantaneous without saying when the pseudo-first-order result stops being valid. E ≈ Ha holds only while Ha is well below E∞; near Ha ≈ E∞ the reaction plane forms and E levels off at E∞ even though k is large.
fix: Add the condition: the fast pseudo-first-order regime needs 3 < Ha << E∞. As Ha approaches E∞, E saturates at E∞ = 1 + (D_B·C_B)/(b·D_A·C_Ai) and stops rising with k.
